# Added Anan-AS PVM Interpreter

## Pull Request by @DrEverr

Created interface fo external interpreters.
Changed HostCallRegister, HCMemory and GasCounter API.
Added Ananas as second possible backend to run services on.
Added flag `--pvm` to choose pvm backend for accumulate execution.
Currently supported backends: ['built-in', 'ananas'].

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added support for multiple PVM backend implementations (BuiltIn and Ananas).
  * Introduced configurable PVM backend selection via `--pvm` command-line option and configuration files.
  * Enabled parallel execution of multiple interpreter engines for enhanced testing and validation.

* **Chores**
  * Reorganized core VM infrastructure into separate interface and implementation packages for improved modularity.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Walkthrough

Adds a PVM backend abstraction and multiplatform PVM support across the repo. Introduces packages/core/pvm-interface and packages/core/pvm-interpreter-ananas, an IPvmInterpreter interface, and an Ananas WASM-backed interpreter implementation. Refactors the existing interpreter to implement the new interface, replaces many local gas/memory/register APIs with interface types (IGasCounter, IMemory, IRegisters, HostCallMemory, HostCallRegisters), and threads a new PvmBackend enum and CLI `--pvm` option through jam, importer, workers, and transition code. Accumulate and related host-calls are adapted for backend selection and async executor creation; many tests updated for multi-backend runs.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~60 minutes

Areas requiring extra attention:
- packages/core/pvm-interpreter/interpreter.ts — public API reshaping to IPvmInterpreter, new resetJam/resetGeneric, public registers/memory/gas fields.
- packages/core/pvm-host-calls/host-calls.ts and interpreter-instance-manager.ts — migration to IPvmInterpreter, runProgram/resetJam flow, instance manager factory and async lifecycle.
- packages/core/pvm-interpreter-ananas/index.ts — new WASM interpreter wrapper (reset/run/step/gas/registers/memory integration).
- packages/jam/transition/accumulate/pvm-executor.ts and accumulate.ts — async factory methods, PvmBackend plumbing, createAccumulateExecutor signature changes.
- Wide, repetitive type/import migrations (IGasCounter, HostCallMemory/HostCallRegisters, pvm-interface imports) — verify all import sources and downstream callsites.

## Possibly related PRs

- FluffyLabs/typeberry#337 — related host-call memory/register abstraction changes and HostCallMemory/HostCallRegisters refactor.
- FluffyLabs/typeberry#451 — overlapping changes to the accumulate execution pipeline and PvmExecutor/createAccumulateExecutor signatures.
- FluffyLabs/typeberry#505 — related gas counter behavior and gas tests adjustments.

## Comment by @tomusdrw

> But does this benchmark run on ananas?

Don't think so. It's just running on whatever is default for `fuzz-target`. So with benchmarks at https://github.com/FluffyLabs/typeberry/pull/716#issuecomment-3426102168 we see current improvement compared to the latest released version that is already on `main`.

If you change the default for typeberry to be `ananas` in this PR we can run the benchmarks again and then be able to compare the two.

## Comment by @tomusdrw

To reduce back and forth between JS and WASM and keep the API simple, we should just use `getRegisters()` and `setRegisters()` API, where we can set multiple registers in one go.

## Comment by @tomusdrw

Looking from the interface perspective I still disagree.
1. We pass `initialGas` to `reset*` method.
2. At any point in time we can get `instance.getGasCounter().get()` to see the remaining gas.
3. Why is `getGasConsumed()` needed to be implemented separately? Can it ever be different in value? It seems to me, it does exactly the same thing for all cases - just takes the initial gas and subtracts the current gas (handling potential underflow).

I really think it shouldn't need to be duplicated in the interface (and in each and every implementation). My suggestion would be to add `initialGas` (getter-only/readonly property) to `GasCounter` interface. Or if it's really easier to have it computed internally, we should have `GasCounter.getConsumedGas()` and `GasCounter.getGasLeft()` methods.

This method just doesn't fit `PvmInterface` given there is rich `GasCounter` interface already in place. Having multiple ways of doing the same thing (i.e. computing how much gas is left by using this method or subtracting remaining gas from the initial gas) introduces confusion during usage and unnecessary complexity for interface implementations.

## Comment by @tomusdrw

This is pretty suboptimal and something that I'd rather avoid. Now each  time we read a single register we need to fetch all registers from WASM context.

Registers are needed only for host calls and I'd rather see:
```ts
IPvmInterface {
  getEncodedRegisters(): Uint8Array
  setEncodedRegisters(r: Uint8Array): void;
}
```
top-level API. That way we simply fetch registers before executing a hostcall and then set all changes back when the host call is done (before resuming execution).

After you fetch registers feel free to create some sort of buffered register viewer:
```ts
class Registers {
  private readonly view: BigUint64Array;
  constructor(public readonly encoded: Uint8Array) {
    this.view = new BigUint64Array(encoded);
  }
  // note usage of `RegisterIndex` here - we make the user of the API responsible for making sure that the index is within bounds.
  get(index: RegisterIndex): U64 {
    return tryAsU64(this.view.get(index));
  }
  set(index: RegisterIndex, value: U64): void {
     this.view.set(index, value);
   }
}
```

## Comment by @tomusdrw

It's right below the link you posted:
https://graypaper.fluffylabs.dev/#/ab2cdbd/25ed0025ed00?v=0.7.2

Memory access is `mod 2*32` which is equivalent to just taking `lowerU32`. So, yes, everytime we access memory we just take lower u32 part of the register.
Accessing reserved memory (first 16 pages) always yields a panic.

       * Create entire readable pages to handle the `[start, end)` range.
       *
       * Note that both `start` and `end` must be multiple of the `PAGE_SIZE`, i.e.
       * they need to be the start indices of the pages.
       *
       * The data passed will be placed at `start`, but might be shorter than the requested range,
       * prepend it with zeros if you don't wish to have it at the beginning of the page.
       */
      setReadablePages(start: MemoryIndex, end: MemoryIndex, data: Uint8Array = new Uint8Array()) {
        this.ensureNotFinalized();
        check`${start < end} end has to be bigger than start`;
        check`${start % PAGE_SIZE === 0} start needs to be a multiple of page size (${PAGE_SIZE})`;
        check`${end % PAGE_SIZE === 0} end needs to be a multiple of page size (${PAGE_SIZE})`;
        check`${data.length <= end - start} the initial data is longer than address range`;

        const length = end - start;
        const range = MemoryRange.fromStartAndLength(start, length);

        this.ensureNoReservedMemoryUsage(range);

        const pages = Array.from(PageRange.fromMemoryRange(range));
        const noOfPages = pages.length;

        for (let i = 0; i < noOfPages; i++) {
          const pageNumber = pages[i];
          const dataChunk = data.subarray(i * PAGE_SIZE, (i + 1) * PAGE_SIZE);
          const page = new ReadablePage(pageNumber, dataChunk);
          this.initialMemory.set(pageNumber, page);
        }

        return this;
      }

      /**
       * Create entire writeable pages to handle the `[start, end)` range.
       *
       * Note that both `start` and `end` must be multiple of the `PAGE_SIZE`, i.e.
       * they need to be the start indices of the pages.
       *
       * The data passed will be placed at `start`, but might be shorter than the requested range,
       * prepend it with zeros if you don't wish to have it at the beginning of the page.
       */
      setWriteablePages(start: MemoryIndex, end: MemoryIndex, data: Uint8Array = new Uint8Array()) {
        this.ensureNotFinalized();
        check`${start < end} end has to be bigger than start`;
        check`${start % PAGE_SIZE === 0} start needs to be a multiple of page size (${PAGE_SIZE})`;
        check`${end % PAGE_SIZE === 0} end needs to be a multiple of page size (${PAGE_SIZE})`;
        check`${data.length <= end - start} the initial data is longer than address range`;

        const length = end - start;
        const range = MemoryRange.fromStartAndLength(start, length);

        this.ensureNoReservedMemoryUsage(range);

        const pages = Array.from(PageRange.fromMemoryRange(range));
        const noOfPages = pages.length;

        for (let i = 0; i < noOfPages; i++) {
          const pageNumber = pages[i];
          const dataChunk = data.subarray(i * PAGE_SIZE, (i + 1) * PAGE_SIZE);
          const page = new WriteablePage(pageNumber, dataChunk);
          this.initialMemory.set(pageNumber, page);
        }

        return this;
      }

      /**
       * This function can be useful when page map and initial memory data are provided separatelly.
       * You can use setWriteablePages/setReadablePages to create empty pages and then setData to fill them
       */
      setData(start: MemoryIndex, data: Uint8Array) {
        this.ensureNotFinalized();
        const pageOffset = start % PAGE_SIZE;
        const remainingSpaceOnPage = PAGE_SIZE - pageOffset;
        check`${data.length <= remainingSpaceOnPage} The data has to fit into a single page.`;

        const length = data.length;
        const range = MemoryRange.fromStartAndLength(start, length);

        this.ensureNoReservedMemoryUsage(range);

        const pageNumber = getPageNumber(start);
        const page = this.initialMemory.get(pageNumber);

        if (page === undefined) {
          throw new PageNotExist();
        }

        const startPageIndex = tryAsPageIndex(start - page.start);
        page.setData(startPageIndex, data);

        return this;
      }

      finalize(startHeapIndex: MemoryIndex, endHeapIndex: SbrkIndex): Memory {
        check`
          ${startHeapIndex <= endHeapIndex}
          startHeapIndex (${startHeapIndex}) has to be less than or equal to endHeapIndex (${endHeapIndex})
        `;
        this.ensureNotFinalized();

        const heapRange = MemoryRange.fromStartAndLength(startHeapIndex, endHeapIndex - startHeapIndex);
        const heapPagesRange = PageRange.fromMemoryRange(heapRange);
        const initializedPageNumbers = Array.from(this.initialMemory.keys());

        for (const pageNumber of initializedPageNumbers) {
          if (heapPagesRange.isInRange(pageNumber)) {
            throw new IncorrectSbrkIndex();
          }
        }

        const memory = Memory.fromInitialMemory({
          memory: this.initialMemory,
          sbrkIndex: tryAsSbrkIndex(startHeapIndex),
          endHeapIndex,
        });

        this.isFinalized = true;
        return memory;
      }
    }

    export class Registers implements IRegisters {
      private asSigned: BigInt64Array;
      private asUnsigned: BigUint64Array;

      constructor(private readonly bytes = safeAllocUint8Array(NO_OF_REGISTERS << REGISTER_SIZE_SHIFT)) {
        check`${bytes.length === NO_OF_REGISTERS << REGISTER_SIZE_SHIFT} Invalid size of registers array.`;
        this.asSigned = new BigInt64Array(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset);
        this.asUnsigned = new BigUint64Array(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset);
      }

      getAllEncoded(): Uint8Array {
        return this.bytes;
      }

      setAllEncoded(bytes: Uint8Array): void {
        check`${bytes.length === this.bytes.length} Incorrect size of input registers. Got: ${bytes.length}, need: ${this.bytes.length}`;
        this.bytes.set(bytes, 0);
      }

      static fromBytes(bytes: Uint8Array) {
        check`${bytes.length === NO_OF_REGISTERS << REGISTER_SIZE_SHIFT} Invalid size of registers array.`;
        return new Registers(bytes);
      }

      getBytesAsLittleEndian(index: number, len: number) {
        const offset = index << REGISTER_SIZE_SHIFT;
        return this.bytes.subarray(offset, offset + len);
      }

      copyFrom(regs: Registers | BigUint64Array) {
        const array = regs instanceof BigUint64Array ? regs : regs.asUnsigned;
        this.asUnsigned.set(array);
      }

      reset() {
        for (let i = 0; i < NO_OF_REGISTERS; i++) {
          this.asUnsigned[i] = 0n;
        }
      }

      getLowerU32(registerIndex: number) {
        return Number(this.asUnsigned[registerIndex] & 0xff_ff_ff_ffn);
      }

      getLowerI32(registerIndex: number) {
        return Number(this.getLowerU32(registerIndex)) >> 0;
      }

      setU32(registerIndex: number, value: number) {
        this.asUnsigned[registerIndex] = signExtend32To64(value);
      }

      setI32(registerIndex: number, value: number) {
        this.asSigned[registerIndex] = signExtend32To64(value);
      }

      getU64(registerIndex: number) {
        return this.asUnsigned[registerIndex];
      }

      getI64(registerIndex: number) {
        return this.asSigned[registerIndex];
      }

      setU64(registerIndex: number, value: bigint) {
        this.asUnsigned[registerIndex] = value;
      }

      setI64(registerIndex: number, value: bigint) {
        this.asSigned[registerIndex] = value;
      }

      getAllU64() {
        return this.asUnsigned;
      }
    }

    export function safeAllocUint8Array(length: number) {
      if (length > MAX_LENGTH) {
        // biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noConsole: can't have a dependency on logger here
        console.warn(`Trying to allocate ${length} bytes, which is greater than the maximum of ${MAX_LENGTH}.`);
      }
      return new Uint8Array(Math.min(MAX_LENGTH, length));
    }
